title: Thresholds and consequences
goals: Apply a declared score threshold including equality
Compare false alarms and misses at two thresholds
Separate validation choices from final testing
vocabulary: A model output used to rank or decide
A boundary that converts a score to a label
A positive prediction for a negative reference
A declared way to value different mistakes

blocks.text: A classifier score is not automatically a probability. Declare blocked positive and predict blocked when score is at least the threshold. Changing this boundary changes decisions without necessarily retraining the model. Select it using development evidence and a task-relevant rule, not final-test answers.

Use fictional classroom data throughout this investigation. Keep the task, units, reference labels and data split visible as you reason. Earlier weeks supplied the model-building process; this week examines thresholds and consequences.

Six records have score/reference pairs A .9/blocked, B .7/clear, C .6/blocked, D .4/blocked, E .3/clear, F .1/clear. At threshold .5, TP=2, FP=1, FN=1, TN=2. At .3, TP=3, FP=2, FN=0, TN=1. Equality is positive, so E is flagged at .3.

blocks.title: Python 3 check
blocks.text:
scores = [0.9, 0.7, 0.6, 0.4, 0.3, 0.1]
actual = [True, False, True, True, False, False]
for threshold in [0.5, 0.3]:
    predicted = [s >= threshold for s in scores]
    fp = sum(p and not a for p, a in zip(predicted, actual))
    fn = sum(not p and a for p, a in zip(predicted, actual))
    print(threshold, fp, fn, fp + 4 * fn)
# Output rows: 0.5 1 1 5, then 0.3 2 0 2.

Trace the calculation on paper before running this optional Python check. Use the stated fictional inputs and compare intermediate values. The code checks this example; your independent workbook case uses different evidence.

blocks.title: Thresholds and consequences at a glance
blocks.caption: Lowering the threshold here finds D but adds E as a false alarm. The two accuracies are equal while consequences differ. Precision is 2/3 at .5 and 3/5 at .3; recall rises from 2/3 to 1. This behavior follows these fixed scores and records, not a promise of future performance.

blocks.label: Give TP, FP, FN, TN at both thresholds. Explain the steps or evidence behind your response.

blocks.text: Suppose the classroom cost is one point per false alarm and four per miss. Total costs are 5 at .5 and 2 at .3, so .3 wins among these two candidates under this rule. If false alarms cost four and misses cost one, costs are 5 and 8, reversing the choice.

These invented costs support arithmetic practice, not real robot deployment. Stakeholders must justify actual consequences. Record every tried threshold and retain a separate final test; a threshold is part of the selected method.

blocks.label: Why not select the threshold with the lowest final-test cost?

workbook.title: Apply the boundary
workbook.prompt: Which IDs are positive at .5 and .3?
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: At .5: A, B, C. At .3: A, B, C, D, E, including equality.

workbook.title: Count the consequences
workbook.prompt: Give TP, FP, FN, TN at both thresholds.

workbook.title: Use the declared cost
workbook.prompt: Calculate costs with FP cost 1 and FN cost 4.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Costs are 1+4=5 and 2+0=2; .3 is preferred among these candidates.

workbook.title: Apply independently
workbook.prompt: Scores/references are .8/blocked,.5/clear,.2/blocked,.1/clear. Compare thresholds .5 and .2 using the same cost.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: At .5 TP 1 FP 1 FN 1 TN 1 cost 5. At .2 TP 2 FP 1 FN 0 TN 1 cost 1. Equality is positive at both boundaries.

workbook.title: Protect the final test
workbook.prompt: Why not select the threshold with the lowest final-test cost?
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Selection uses the test answers, turning the test into development data and weakening its independent evaluation role.

teacher.background: Teach two 45-minute sessions. This week focuses on thresholds and consequences. Model the worked example first, collect the new W 4 case independently before feedback, and use the fresh retry to check transfer. Award credit for traceable reasoning and bounded claims, including justified uncertainty.
materials: Paper, pencils and a calculator for fractions
The fictional examples and a blank evidence table
Optional Python 3 editor; no external packages or AI accounts required
sessions: Use the prerequisite question: Which denominator defines recall? Check the explanation before proceeding.
Read the opening and model the worked evidence. Ask students to identify score in context.
Complete W 1 and W 2 with support: apply the boundary; count the consequences. Require the evidence, not only the final response.
Read the visual row by row. Collect the guided explanation and compare reasoning in pairs. Trace the Python check after the paper calculation.
Retrieve the distinction between score and threshold. Invite a counterexample to an overconfident claim.
Discuss the application and complete W 3: Calculate costs with FP cost 1 and FN cost 4.
Collect W4 independently before giving hints. Assess these outcomes: Apply a declared score threshold including equality; Compare false alarms and misses at two thresholds. Record any support used.
Use W 5 and the exit response to assess limits. Give targeted feedback, then the fresh retry. Save evidence of independent understanding.
teacher.guidedAnswer: Guided response: At .5: 2, 1, 1, 2. At .3: 3, 2, 0, 1. Exit response: Selection uses the test answers, turning the test into development data and weakening its independent evaluation role.
misconceptions: Ask for the relevant counts, units, procedure or saved record. For this week: At .5: A, B, C. At .3: A, B, C, D, E, including equality.

teacher.assessment: For independent W 4, require: At .5 TP 1 FP 1 FN 1 TN 1 cost 5. At .2 TP 2 FP 1 FN 0 TN 1 cost 1. Equality is positive at both boundaries. Fresh retry .9/clear,.6/blocked,.4/clear,.2/blocked at threshold .4: TP 1 FP 2 FN 1 TN 0, cost 6 under FP 1 FN 4. Require equality and all counts. Mark each criterion as independent, supported or not yet demonstrated. Reassess the reasoning after feedback; do not replace the first attempt silently.
teacher.support: Provide a blank evidence table and allow a verbal explanation before writing. Highlight the given conditions without supplying the W 4 conclusion. Use score and threshold in full sentences. Extension: alter one condition in the worked example and explain which conclusion changes and which remains supported.
